correctness.rationale: For any field, the explicit exponent polytope \(P=[0,2]^3\) intersect \(2\le a+b+c\le3\) has 13 integer points, exactly one more than the 12 selected generators. Full-rank column differences have determinant one; a unit-cube subdivision into unimodular tetrahedra proves IDP in every degree. Four explicit degree-two replacement identities remove the missing generator from every product of length ≥2, so the normalization quotient is exactly \(k(-1)\). Hochster normal-semigroup Cohen–Macaulayness and the short exact sequence give depth \(1\), \(H^1\)=\(k(-1)\), and normal Proj; inclusion-exclusion counts every graded monomial and gives the claimed Hilbert series and degree. Actual included verify.py independently checks replacements, determinants, and graded counts through degree 8 (VERIFY_OK); finite checks are corroboration rather than infinite proof.

value.rationale: The original 12-cubic example is a natural named osculating-defective toric threefold with long-standing questions about arithmetic Cohen–Macaulayness of Togliatti systems. An exact *single* gap between its coordinate ring and normalization sharply distinguishes normal projective geometry from non-projectively-normal embedding, forces the maximal possible graded-depth failure (depth \(1\) in dimension 4), gives the entire deficiency module and all-degree Hilbert function, and is not a routine consequence of the original Laplace or singularity discussion. This object-specific structural classification plausibly informs comparison of Togliatti embeddings and their syzygy/cohomological invariants.
